did: An ideation session about Korean, with no code. It began with what 'because it rained, I stayed home' is called in Korean grammar and ended as one design. All Korean practice happens in one drama world where every scene stands alone, and every session is memoryless. It has four parts. Shop: say a hunch in English and find the phrases and scenes that do it, from a library you own. Mine: catch a native speaker saying a phrase in a real clip. Focus: each scene declares what it teaches, and code proves it. Play: listen to the setup and the scene, then reach for the phrase in a new situation, in Korean or English. A model only writes text ahead of time, code checks everything, and the voice is AI with labelled native spans. It was filed as epic KPLAY with ten stories and two asks. TALK8 was folded into it, and #1986's sources question is answered there.
